question: Why is a stack the right structure for matching brackets, rather than one counter per bracket kind?
options: Counters are slower than a stack
Only the most recently opened bracket may close next, so order matters and counters lose it
A stack uses less memory than three integers
why: Counters accept "([)]" because every kind balances out. The stack remembers the order of the unclosed openers, which is exactly the last-in, first-out rule of the problem.
